sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk increases with more delinquencies.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies: it adds much more risk for applicants who have had delinquencies than for those who have not.
Income is among the third or fourth most important drivers, and higher income decreases default risk.
Length of credit history is also among the third or fourth most important drivers, and longer histories decrease default risk.
Debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, and risk increases with it.
The data do not settle whether the number of dependents matters, since no movement in its curve is resolved at this sample size.
Recent credit inquiries have at most a weak effect, and applicant age hardly matters.
